- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or erratic, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 1–3% to forecast to reflect potential breakout.
